[conn.sugar_liver]

[conn.vitd_alp]
phrase: Your vitamin D is low and one bone-linked enzyme is raised. The two often go together, because bone turns over faster when vitamin D runs short.

today: Usually nothing.
why: Albumin is the main protein your liver makes. It falls when the liver makes less, when protein is lost through the kidneys or the gut, when the body is inflamed, or when food has been short of protein for a while. One reading cannot say which.
do: This needs a deeper look, starting with a repeat test.

[finding.b12_low.A]

today: Often nothing. Sometimes tiredness, or pins and needles in the hands or feet.
why: B12 comes almost entirely from animal foods, so it runs low in vegetarians, and in anyone who absorbs it poorly. Acid-lowering medicines and metformin are common reasons.
do: Dairy, eggs and fortified foods help. It is read again at your next test.

[finding.bilirubin.B]

[finding.crp.A]

today: Nothing you would feel.

do: Sleep, movement and less processed food usually bring it down.
summary: Background inflammation, in the middle zone.

[finding.crp.B]

today: Nothing you would feel.

do: Consider reading it again in a few weeks, when you are well and rested. If it is still raised, it needs a deeper look for where it is coming from.

[finding.egfr_low.C]
head: Your kidney filtering figure appears to be below 60, the line at which it is usually checked again.
today: Nothing you would feel.
why: This figure is worked out from your creatinine, your age and your sex. It estimates how much blood your kidneys clean each minute, and it falls slowly with age. One reading below 60 cannot say whether it will hold: too little water, a hard workout or a high-protein meal before the test can sometimes lower it.
do: A repeat test, with a urine test alongside it, is the usual first step.
summary: Kidney filtering figure, below 60.
closing: A result this far outside its range needs a doctor's attention. Please speak to your doctor.

[finding.hcy.A]
head: Your homocysteine sits just above its range.
today: Nothing you would feel.
why: Homocysteine is a by-product the body clears with the help of B vitamins. High levels go with artery disease, though bringing the number down has not been shown to prevent it. The useful question is why it is raised.
do: Leafy greens, pulses and eggs supply the vitamins that clear it. It is read again at your next test.
summary: Homocysteine, just above its range. Read again at your next test.

[finding.lpa.B]
head: One inherited part of your heart picture appears to be clearly raised.
today: Nothing you would feel.
why: Lp(a) is a cholesterol particle set almost entirely by your genes. Food and exercise barely move it. A raised level adds to whatever the other numbers carry, so the other numbers matter more for you than for most people.
do: Keep the rest of this section as good as it can be. It runs in families, so it is worth telling yours.
summary: Lp(a), an inherited particle, just above the line. Nothing to do.
closing: A result at this level is worth mentioning at your next routine check-up.
page 1 step: 

[finding.lpa.C]
head: One inherited part of your heart picture appears to be far above the line.
today: Nothing you would feel.
why: Lp(a) is a cholesterol particle set almost entirely by your genes. Food and exercise barely move it. At this level it can be a risk of its own, whatever the other numbers say.
do: Keep the rest of this section as good as it can be. It runs in families, so it is worth telling yours.
summary: Lp(a), an inherited particle, just above the line. Nothing to do.
closing: A level this high needs a doctor's attention, because there are things a doctor can do about the overall risk. Please speak to your doctor.

[finding.metals.A]
head: {names} {is_are} above {its_their} limit.
today: Usually nothing.
why: Blood levels mostly reflect the last few weeks: a fish meal can raise mercury and arsenic, and smoking raises cadmium. A raised level that holds on a repeat means more is coming in than the body is clearing, and the work is to find the source. Water, cookware, cosmetics, traditional remedies and the workplace are the usual ones.
do: This needs a deeper look: tracing the source is the first step.
summary: 
closing:

[finding.phosphorus_low.A]
head: Your phosphorus sits just below its range.
today: Nothing you would feel.
why: Phosphorus works with calcium and vitamin D in bone and muscle. A reading a little below the range, with calcium in range, usually means little.
do: It is read again at your next test, alongside your vitamin D.
summary: Phosphorus, just below its range. Read again at your next test.
closing: 
page 1 step: 

[finding.phosphorus_low.B]
head: Your phosphorus appears to be clearly low.
today: Nothing you would feel.
why: Phosphorus works with calcium and vitamin D in bone and muscle. A low reading can sometimes follow low vitamin D, some medicines or eating very little. A repeat shows whether it holds.
do: Consider a repeat test, alongside your calcium and vitamin D.
summary: Phosphorus, just below its range. Read again at your next test.
closing: A result at this level is worth mentioning at your next routine check-up.

[finding.phosphorus_low.C]

today: Often nothing. Marked muscle weakness would be a reason not to wait.
why: Phosphorus works with calcium and vitamin D in bone and muscle. A reading this low usually has a reason, and it is worth finding.
do: A repeat test in the coming days is the usual first step.

[finding.platelets_high.A]
head: Your platelet count sits just above its range.
today: Nothing you would feel.
why: Platelets are the cells that help blood clot. A count a little above the range often follows an infection, low iron or inflammation somewhere in the body. A repeat shows whether it was passing.
do: It is read again at your next test.
summary: Platelets, just above their range. Read again at your next test.
closing:

[finding.platelets_high.C]
head: Your platelet count appears to be far above its range.
today: Nothing you would feel.
why: Platelets are the cells that help blood clot. A count this high can sometimes follow an infection, low iron or inflammation, and occasionally the body is making too many. It is worth finding the reason.
do: A repeat test in the coming days is the usual first step, with a look at the reason.
summary: Platelets, just above their range. Read again at your next test.
closing: A result this far outside its range needs a doctor's attention. Please speak to your doctor.

today: Nothing you would feel.
why: The size, number and evenness of red cells shift when iron, B12 or folate run low, sometimes before haemoglobin does. Being a little dry on the morning of the test can also raise the count.

summary: One red cell measure, just outside its range. Read again at your next test.

[finding.salts.A]
head: One of your body's salts sits outside its range.
today: Nothing you would feel.
why: Sodium, potassium and calcium are held in a narrow band, so even a small move is marked. The way a sample is handled on its way to the laboratory can raise potassium falsely, and some medicines move all three.
do: It is read again at your next test.
summary: One salt, just outside its range. Read again at your next test.
closing:

[finding.sugar.A]
head: Your sugar sits just above the line.
today: You may notice nothing at all.
why: Your body is working a little harder than it should to handle sugar. This is the stage where it turns around most easily.
do: What is on the plate and when, and a walk after your largest meal.
summary: Your sugar, just above the line.
closing: 
page 1 step: Bringing your <a href="#sugar">sugar average</a> down through what is on the plate and when, movement after meals, and sleep.

[finding.sugar.B]
head: Your sugar appears to be clearly above the line.
today: Many people feel nothing. Some notice a dip in energy after meals, or more thirst than usual.
why: Laboratories mark this range as prediabetes. At this level the body may be struggling to keep sugar in line, and it tends to drift upward if nothing changes. It is also the stage where food, movement and sleep change the number most.
do: This is the first thing to work on: what is on the plate and when, movement after meals, and sleep.
summary: Your sugar, clearly above the line.
closing: A result at this level is worth mentioning at your next routine check-up.
page 1 step: Bringing your <a href="#sugar">sugar average</a> down through what is on the plate and when, movement after meals, and sleep.

[finding.sugar.C]
head: Your sugar appears to be well above the line.
today: Some people feel tired, thirsty or pass urine more often. Many feel nothing.
why: Laboratories mark this range as diabetes, and one reading is usually confirmed with a second. The three-month average can also read falsely high or low with anaemia or an inherited haemoglobin trait. Food, movement and sleep still matter a great deal, and they are the part we can work on.
do: What is on the plate and when, movement after meals, and sleep. If you already take medicine for sugar, do not change it because of this report.
summary: Your sugar, well above the line.
closing: A result this far outside its range needs a doctor's attention. Please speak to your doctor.
page 1 step: Bringing your <a href="#sugar">sugar average</a> down through what is on the plate and when, movement after meals, and sleep.

[finding.tg.A]
head: The fat travelling in your blood sits just above the line.
today: Nothing you would feel.
why: Triglycerides rise with sugar, refined carbohydrate and alcohol more than with fat, and they fall quickly when those change. Raised for years, they add to the load on your arteries.
do: Less sugar, refined carbohydrate and alcohol, and a walk after meals. This number often moves within weeks.
summary: Triglycerides, the fat travelling in your blood, just above the line.
closing: 
page 1 step: Bringing your <a href="#heart">triglycerides</a> down: less sugar, refined carbohydrate and alcohol, and a walk after meals.

summary: Triglycerides, the fat travelling in your blood, clearly raised.

do: Less sugar, refined carbohydrate and alcohol, and a walk after meals. This number often moves within weeks.

[finding.tsh_low.A]
head: The signal asking your thyroid to work sits just below its range.
today: Nothing you would feel.
why: A low signal means the brain is asking for less thyroid hormone than usual. Just below the range it is often a passing dip.
do: A repeat in two to three months shows whether it has settled. Biotin, found in hair and nail supplements, can make this test read falsely low, so mention it if you take any.
summary: Thyroid signal, just below its range. Read again at your next test.
closing: 
page 1 step: 

[finding.uric.A]
head: Your uric acid sits just above its range.
today: Nothing you would feel.
why: Uric acid rises with sweet drinks, alcohol, red meat and shellfish, and with sugar strain in general. High for long enough, it can settle in joints.
do: More water, fewer sweet drinks and less alcohol usually bring it down.
summary: Uric acid, just above its range.
closing: 
page 1 step: Bringing your <a href="#sugar">uric acid</a> down: more water, fewer sweet drinks, less alcohol.

[finding.vitd_high.B]
head: Your vitamin D is above its range.
today: Nothing you would feel.
why: This almost always comes from supplements. More is not better with vitamin D: too much pulls calcium into the blood.
do: Note what you are taking and how much, and do not stop anything a doctor prescribed without asking them.
summary: Vitamin D, above its range.
closing: A result at this level is worth mentioning at your next routine check-up.

[finding.vitd_low.A]
head: Your vitamin D is a little short of where it should be.
today: Nothing you would feel at this level.
why: Vitamin D is made in the skin from sunlight, and bones, muscles and the immune system all need it. Most people who work indoors run low.
do: Some sun on bare arms and legs, most days, is where to start.
summary: Vitamin D, a little short.
closing: 
page 1 step: Building your <a href="#nutrients">vitamin D</a> back up, starting with some sun most days.

[finding.white_cells.A]
head: Your white cells sit outside their range.
today: Nothing you would feel.
why: White cells rise with an infection or stress on the body, and can dip for a few weeks after a viral illness. A repeat shows whether it was passing.
do: It is read again at your next test.
summary: White cells, just outside their range. Read again at your next test.
